title: security(rbac-v2): enforce KMS region pinning + audit hardening
author: Alex Chen
description: Context: customers have requested stronger guarantees that customer-managed keys (KMS) are only used in allowed regions and that RBAC v2 policies enforce this at request-time rather than relying on post-hoc audit. This PR implements enforcement for KMS region pinning across the control plane, enriches audit logs with residency metadata, and hardens RBAC v2 policy checks to return deterministic errors and metrics for observability. Motivation: reduce accidental cross-region KMS usage, provide clear audit trails for compliance, and surface policy violations as metrics/alerts. Changes: 1) Add a KMS region residency constraint to the RBAC v2 policy engine (policy rule + evaluator + config). 2) Enforce region pinning in the KMS integration layer with fail-fast behavior for disallowed regions. 3) Enrich audit events with kms_region and policy_evaluation fields; include before/after key material references (obfuscated). 4) Add a migration to populate existing KMS key metadata and backfill residency annotations where available. 5) Add end-to-end integration tests and unit tests for policy permutations. 6) Update docs and admin console policy UI copy. Rollout plan: feature gated behind org-level flag "rbac_v2_kms_residency_enforce" for two weeks, start in audit mode by default for existing customers, flip to enforce for new organizations. Monitoring: new telemetry metrics (rbac.v2.kms_policy_violation.count, audit.kms_region_mismatch.count) added and dashboard panels in Redwood Console. Backwards compatibility: when flag is off, behavior is unchanged (audit-only). See linked Linear tasks for rollout automated job.
